name: Max Tagher
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Mercury (Mercury Technologies Inc.)
profile: Max Tagher co-founded San Francisco fintech Mercury in 2017 with Immad Akhund and Jason Zhang and serves as its CTO. Mercury offers banking services to startups and small businesses through partner banks and was valued at about $5.2B as of 2026.
interesting_fact: Mercury's entire backend is written in Haskell, an unusual choice for a startup; Tagher says Haskell's correctness suited building the core features of a bank, and that backend Haskell engineer is the company's 'easiest role to hire for'.
deep_cut_fact: Tagher credits Michael Snoyman's open-source Yesod and Persistent libraries, saying Mercury 'would have never used Haskell if not for his work'; he personally tries to sponsor the OSS authors of the ~194 packages Mercury depends on.
notes: Engineering-focused, low public profile compared with CEO Immad Akhund; Haskell/engineering angle is the natural hook.

name: Megan Bent
profile: Could not verify any Megan Bent as a founder of Uplight. Uplight was formed in 2019 by merging Colorado cleantech firms Tendril and Simple Energy (founders include Adrian Tuck of Tendril and Yoav Lurie/Justin Segall of Simple Energy). The only prominent Megan Bent found is the Boulder-area founder of Harbinger Ventures, a consumer-brand investor with no verified Uplight link.
notes: Likely a data error in the source list (Hurun). Uplight leadership page lists Tendril/Simple Energy founders, not Megan Bent: https://uplight.com/blog/uplight-executive-team/ . Harbinger Ventures' Megan Bent bio: https://hirshberginstitute.com/megan-bent/ . Verify before outreach.

name: Amir Nathoo
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Outschool (stepped back as CEO in Feb 2026; Brian Co named CEO Sept 2026)
profile: UK-raised, Cambridge-educated engineer who worked at IBM, co-founded mobile dev platform Trigger.io (acquired by Square in 2013), then co-founded Outschool in 2015, a marketplace for live online classes for kids valued at $3B in 2021. In Feb 2026 he stepped back from leading Outschool to start 'a new personal journey'.
interesting_fact: Outschool says it has offered 100,000+ live online classes to over 1 million learners in 196 countries, and Nathoo set aside equity in the company for teachers' benefit.
deep_cut_fact: After Square acquired his startup Trigger.io in 2013, Nathoo spent about 15 months there as a product manager and founded a new product line, Square Payroll, before leaving in 2015 to start Outschool.
notes: Now between roles after leaving the CEO job; may be more open to podcast invites. No published personal/press email found.

name: Sugawara Junichi
current_role: Co-founder, Director and Representative Executive Officer, Spiber Inc.
profile: Junichi Sugahara (Sugawara in the source list) co-founded Spiber in 2007 in Tsuruoka, Yamagata, with Kazuhide Sekiyama out of Keio University's Institute for Advanced Biosciences. Spiber develops fermentation-made 'Brewed Protein' fibres and materials for fashion and other industries; he became Representative Executive Officer in 2023.
interesting_fact: Sugahara and Sekiyama were named to the Vogue Business 2025 100 Innovators list (Entrepreneurs and Founders category) for Spiber's protein-based materials.
deep_cut_fact: Spiber started in 2007 as student research at Keio's Tsuruoka biosciences lab under Prof. Masaru Tomita: Sugahara (then a second-year student) and Sekiyama analysed silk from several spider species to decode its amino-acid sequences.
notes: Name usually romanised 'Junichi Sugahara' (菅原潤一). Co-founder Sekiyama is the more public face; Sugahara holds a Keio PhD and has also led Spiber investee Synplogen (per MarketScreener, unverified on primary source).

name: Navdeep (Navi) Chadha
profile: Navi Chadha co-founded Axtria in 2010 with his brother Jassi Chadha (CEO); the company provides AI-powered data analytics and cloud software to the life sciences industry. He previously co-founded pharma analytics firm marketRx, acquired by Cognizant in 2007, and has 20+ years in pharma analytics.
interesting_fact: He has been recognised as an EY Entrepreneur of the Year and a Top Industry Leader by Life Sciences Voice; his mantra for pharma AI is 'start with the data foundation, not with the AI.'
deep_cut_fact: Outside work he runs Spartan obstacle races, rides both a bicycle and his Harley, plays golf and skis; the family dog is an Australian Labradoodle named Bear (pharmaphorum '12 Questions', May 2026).
notes: connect@axtria.com is Axtria's general contact address. Pharmaphorum interview invites readers to connect with him on LinkedIn.

name: Naama Alon
current_role: Co-founder and Chief of Product, HoneyBook (per 2021 Calcalist profile; title varies across sources)
profile: Israeli designer who co-founded HoneyBook with Oz Alon (CEO) and Dror Shimoni; it makes client-management and payments software for US freelancers and small creative businesses, and was valued at about $2.4B in 2021. Alon leads product and creative and is based between the Bay Area and Tel Aviv.
interesting_fact: HoneyBook was her idea: it grew out of a college project she started while studying at Shenkar College, and the founders quit their jobs the day after she said they had to commit to it full time.
deep_cut_fact: Before HoneyBook she was a graphic designer and party-thrower on the Tel Aviv party scene; her only job as an employee was at the design studio Red Interactive. She has said: 'I don't want to be the CEO, I'm looking to influence and lead.'
notes: Very private by her own account ('prefers to stay behind the scenes'); her husband and co-founder Oz Alon is the public face, so outreach via HoneyBook/Oz is likely more effective. No published press email found on honeybook.com.

name: Joel Gottsegen
current_role: Co-founder, Qualia (current operating role not confirmed; Nate Baker is CEO)
profile: Joel Gottsegen co-founded Qualia in 2015 with Nate Baker and Lucas Hansen; the company runs a cloud platform connecting homebuyers, sellers, lenders, title/escrow and real-estate agents to digitise the US home-closing process, and was valued around $2B. The co-founders were Forbes 30 Under 30 honorees.
interesting_fact: Qualia was the first technology company to join the Coalition to Stop Real Estate Wire Fraud, and all three co-founders were Forbes 30 Under 30 award recipients.
notes: Very low public profile; aggregator sites suggest a Stanford CS degree and a later venture ('Petty Karma'), but these were not verified from primary sources. Best route is via Qualia press or CEO Nate Baker.

name: Antoine Hubert
current_role: Co-founder of Ynsect (insect-protein company, now defunct); current role not verified
profile: French agricultural engineer (AgroParisTech) who co-founded Ynsect in 2011 with three partners to farm mealworms for animal feed, fertiliser and food protein; it raised over $425M and joined France's Next40. He handed the CEO role to Shankar Krishnamoorthy in 2023 and stayed as an executive VP; Wikipedia lists Ynsect as defunct since Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: MIT Technology Review named him a 2015 Innovator Under 35 for developing 'the first insect biorefinery in the world'; Ynsect chose the mealworm beetle (Tenebrio molitor) as 'nocturnal, flightless' and very high in protein and chitin.
deep_cut_fact: Hubert has compared the insect industry to Norway's aquaculture boom 40 years earlier: 'We are now the same point in the insect industry.' Ynsect's four products from mealworms were protein flour, oil, chitin/chitosan and frass fertiliser.
notes: Ynsect ceased operations (Wikipedia: defunct 1 Dec 2025) - avoid framing outreach around company performance. Current activities unknown; no published contact found. Ynsect page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C3%9Cnsect

name: Mathieu Alengrin
current_role: Co-founder, Ankorstore (listed by Crunchbase as Co-founder and Principal Engineer; not verified on primary source)
profile: French software engineer who was Head of Engineering at Vestiaire Collective before co-founding Ankorstore in Paris in 2019 with Pierre-Louis Lacoste, Nicolas d'Audiffret and Nicolas Cohen. Ankorstore is a European B2B wholesale marketplace connecting independent brands with retailers; it raised a EUR250M Series C in 2022 and reached unicorn status in about two years.
interesting_fact: Ankorstore went from founding in 2019 to unicorn in roughly two years, raising EUR6M seed (2019), EUR25M Series A (2020), EUR84M Series B (2021) and EUR250M Series C (2022).
deep_cut_fact: Ankorstore's founding team paired Alengrin, the engineering lead from luxury resale marketplace Vestiaire Collective, with the founders of the handmade marketplace A Little Market (Nicolas d'Audiffret and Nicolas Cohen) and ex-Etsy Wholesale manager Pierre-Louis Lacoste.
notes: Technical, behind-the-scenes co-founder with almost no press presence; CEO Pierre-Louis Lacoste is the public face. No published press email found on ankorstore.com.

name: Brad Siegler
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder, EquipmentShare (Nasdaq: EQPT); current operating role not confirmed
profile: Missouri-based co-founder of EquipmentShare, the Columbia, Missouri construction-equipment rental and fleet-technology company started by brothers Willy and Jabbok Schlacks with Siegler, Jeff Lowe and Matthew McDonald. Backed early by Y Combinator (2015), EquipmentShare went public on Nasdaq in January 2026; Siegler was listed as a shareholder in the IPO prospectus.
interesting_fact: EquipmentShare grew out of a 2014 Startup Weekend in Columbia, Missouri, where the Schlacks brothers won first place and $2,000; by 2021 it had about 3,000 employees and 90+ locations.
deep_cut_fact: When EquipmentShare went through Y Combinator in 2015, TechCrunch pitched it as 'Airbnb for construction equipment', a peer-to-peer marketplace letting contractors rent idle gear from one another; Siegler was one of three Missouri-area co-founders who joined the Schlacks brothers.
notes: Low public profile. Shareholding confirmed in the 424B4 prospectus (Jan 2026): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1693736/000162828026003334/eqpt-424b4.htm . Wellfound describes him as a UI/UX/web designer and Univ. of Missouri '13 grad (unverified primary).
